title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. College Sunday night review: Ole Miss at Oklahoma (Nov. 15), graded.

paragraphs: Sunday had one college game on the card, Ole Miss at Oklahoma, moved over from Saturday, and it went to the last snap. Oklahoma won 24-17. Oklahoma −2.5 cashed by 4.5 and the Under 48.5 stayed under by 7.5, but only after Oklahoma missed two field goals in the fourth quarter, Ole Miss got an onside kick back with 38 seconds left, and the final throw into the end zone fell incomplete. One catch there ties it at 24 and sends every Ole Miss +2.5 ticket, and every Under ticket, into overtime with their hearts in their throats.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Lock It Up line moves count at their final lines. The Cover Writer's card had Oklahoma −2.5 and the Under 48.5, projecting Oklahoma 26, Ole Miss 19.

Follow The Money rode Oklahoma −2.5 and the Under too. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch took Ole Miss +2.5 and missed. On the total, the Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money had the Under, and The Formula's Over 48.5 fell 7.5 short. In The Trenches had no pick in this one.

items.matchup: College Sunday · Down to the wire

paragraphs: Card line: Oklahoma −2.5, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had Oklahoma −2.5 and the Under, projecting Oklahoma 26, Ole Miss 19. Final: Ole Miss 17, Oklahoma 24. Oklahoma won by 7, and the teams scored 41 points.

Oklahoma −2.5 and the Under 48.5 both cashed, and both had to survive an onside kick and one last throw into the end zone. Oklahoma got the early cushion. Mateer ran 8 yards for a touchdown at 5:54 of the first quarter, and Sategna took an Ole Miss punt back 75 yards for another at 3:29, 14-0. Dye's 19-yard run at 13:27 of the second made it 14-7, and it stayed there through the half: 21 points on the board, and the Under 48.5 crowd feeling fine.

Hatton's 5-yard run at 8:21 of the third made it 21-7, and Oklahoma −2.5 was up 14 with a quarter and a half to go. Then Sandell missed from 39 yards at 13:22 of the fourth, and Ole Miss made the miss hurt. Chambliss ran 32 yards to the Oklahoma 33, then found Odom for a 26-yard touchdown at 11:45. It was 21-14, Oklahoma −2.5 was covering by 4.5, and the Under 48.5 had 35 points with almost 12 minutes left.

Sandell's 41-yard field goal at 4:52 made it 24-14, 38 points. He missed from 51 at 3:04, and Ole Miss drove into Oklahoma territory before a sack at 1:10 pushed it back to the Oklahoma 24. Carneiro's 41-yard field goal at 0:42 made it 24-17, 41 points, and then Fields's onside kick went 10 yards to the Ole Miss 45. Ole Miss had the ball back with 38 seconds left.

Now every Ole Miss +2.5 ticket was alive, because a touchdown and a kick tie it at 24. The Under 48.5 holders were sweating right along with them: a catch and a kick make it 48 points, alive by half a point and headed to overtime, where one more score kills it. Chambliss hit Dye for 15 yards and then for 1 yard to the Oklahoma 29. The last throw, with 5 seconds left, went deep right for Odom in the end zone and fell incomplete. Oklahoma won 24-17, so Oklahoma −2.5 cashed by 4.5, Ole Miss +2.5 missed by 4.5, and the Under 48.5 stayed under by 7.5 at 41.

Called it: The Cover Writer and Follow The Money on Oklahoma −2.5, covered by 4.5 points. The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Under 48.5, stayed under by 7.5 points.
Missed: The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Ole Miss +2.5, missed by 4.5 points. The Formula on the Over 48.5, fell 7.5 points short.
No pick: In The Trenches on the side or the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 1-0 against the spread and 1-0 on totals Sunday, and that runs the week to 40-26-1 against the spread and 28-39 on totals. Oklahoma −2.5 and the Under 48.5 both cashed, and both sweated an onside kick and a last throw into the end zone. That's the best side mark in the room for the week, by itself now, and a totals card that at least closed the week with a winner.

The Formula went 0-1 against the spread and 0-1 on totals Sunday, 34-32-1 and 27-40 for the week. Ole Miss +2.5 and the Over 48.5, and both missed. Still two games over on sides for the week, and the totals mark is the worst in the room. It would rather not discuss it.

Next Man Up went 0-1 against the spread and 1-0 on totals Sunday, 36-30-1 and 36-31 for the week. Ole Miss +2.5 missed, and the Under 48.5 cashed. From the worst side mark in the room on Friday to over .500 on both sides and totals by Sunday night, and it would like everyone to notice.

Letdown Watch went 0-1 against the spread and 1-0 on totals Sunday, 39-27-1 and 32-35 for the week. Ole Miss +2.5 lost and the Under cashed. It was tied with the Cover Writer for the week's side mark going into Sunday and finished one game back. It saw the letdown coming, just not its own.

Follow The Money went 1-0 against the spread and 1-0 on totals Sunday, 12-15 and 25-20 for the week. It moved to Oklahoma −2.5 on the line move and cashed, and the Under 48.5 cashed too. Still under water on sides, but 25-20 is the best totals mark in the room for the week, and the money will remind you.
In The Trenches made no picks Sunday, and it stays 17-22-1 for the week, still with no totals. It sat this one out and will call that discipline.
